transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-11
Start: 15:00 UTC (scheduled)
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Alex Rivera (CTO, Aether); Priya Singh (ML Eng); Samir Das (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be brief):
- High-level parity mapping discussion for models currently on OpenAI/Anthropic/Together
- Console walkthrough focusing on routing, rollouts, and observability

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro — Jordan from Redwood, im the AE, with Maya who is our systems SE, Maya do you want to wave hi?
[00:08] Maya Chen: hi all, Maya here, I'll jump into the runtime and console bits after Jordan sets the stage.
[00:14] Alex Rivera: hey thanks, Alex here. We run Aether DataPort, we do secure data routing for clinical integration, so compliance is a big deal for us.
[00:21] Jordan Patel: great, thanks. The goal today is a parity preview — show how you can map your existing OpenAI and Anthropic calls to Redwood with similar latency and cost profiles and then a short tour of the console Optimize suggestions.
[00:35] Priya Singh: just to flag, our main concern is maintaining throughput for our chat assistants at 95th pct latency under 300ms for short prompts, and keeping cost per 1k tokens under a threshold.
[00:46] Jordan Patel: good, that's exactly the tradeoff we usually run into, maya will explain batching and prefix cache later which helps. A quick question on current infra — Alex, are you running everything through OpenAI hosted endpoints or self-hosted Anthropic?
[00:58] Alex Rivera: primary is OpenAI hosted for most inference, we do a few private Anthropic runs for sensitive data using Anthropic's dedicated endpoints, and we started a tiny pilot with Together for a long-context model for summarization.
[01:12] Maya Chen: okay, that mix is pretty common. For parity mapping we typically map model families to Redwood variants and then tune batch sizes, quantization profile, and KV cache policies.
[01:25] Samir Das: can you explain KV cache again? sometimes i hear K V cash in calls and we want to make sure it's not a billing thing, ha.
[01:31] Maya Chen: (laughs) sure — KV cache is key-value cache, basically we retain transformer key/value states for repeated prefixes so subsequent requests don't recompute from scratch. It reduces token compute and helps latency for multi-turn chat.
[01:44] Priya Singh: does that require session affinity or sticky routing? we do sticky sessions for some flows.
[01:50] Maya Chen: good question — we support both. For hosted, we do logical affinity with a fast routing layer; for Dedicated or Private, you can pin sessions to a pool. We'll show the routing config in the console.
[02:03] Jordan Patel: quick demo plan: 1) show parity mapping doc and live code example for a sample prompt mapping from OpenAI to Redwood API, 2) console tour covering routes, model variants, and rollouts, 3) Optimize recommendations for batching/quant and then Q&A.
[02:18] Maya Chen: jumping into a quick terminal, im going to paste a sample prompt conversion — this is a fairly straightforward mapping, change model identifier, adapt streaming flags, and small response-format differences.
[02:31] Maya Chen: [typing noise] For example, openai call uses completions.create with stop tokens, on Redwood you call /v1/generate with the same prompt but you can attach structured output validators.
[02:44] Priya Singh: are there breaking differences in tokenization between models? we saw differences when moving from gpt-3.5 to gpt-4 equivalent in-house.
[02:52] Maya Chen: tokenization differences happen across model families; Optimize includes a tokenization parity check and suggests prompt rewrites in the parity sheet. We usually ask for a sample prompt set to quantify percent change.
[03:05] Alex Rivera: about streaming — Together's streaming behavior is different, sometimes chunk sizes vary which affects our UI. How does Redwood handle streaming?
[03:14] Maya Chen: Redwood supports server-sent events and per-token streaming, we surfaced chunking controls at the SDK level so you can match your front-end expectations.
[03:24] Samir Das: security — we need to confirm SOC2 and KMS integration, and if logs can be redacted before leaving our VPC.
[03:33] Jordan Patel: yes, we have a security pack; for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS and HSM for key material, plus audit logs that can be pushed to your SIEM. I'll send the SOC2 and encryption docs after the call.
[03:45] Alex Rivera: do you support in-flight encryption with client-side keys or will we have to use gateway-managed keys?
[03:52] Jordan Patel: we support both patterns depending on deployment. Client-side encryption for extremely sensitive payloads is possible on Private. For hosted, we use customer-managed keys via cloud KMS for data-at-rest.
[04:03] Maya Chen: back to performance, here's a slide — we typically achieve parity by tuning three knobs: batching, quantization profile, and KV cache TTLs. Also model selection: picking a Redwood-verified variant that matches the architecture you currently use.
[04:17] Priya Singh: how do you surface the cost impact of quantizing? we need to show financials to finance.
[04:23] Jordan Patel: in the console Optimize tab we show per-token cost breakdown with estimated savings per quant profile and per-batch config. We'll include a sample cost comparison in the parity spreadsheet.
[04:36] Maya Chen: showing the console now — route config, you can set primary model and fallbacks. For example route A uses rwd-llama-13b-fp16 primary and a quantized 8bit fallback for peak offload.
[04:51] Alex Rivera: what about canary rollouts? our product team needs to test on 5% traffic before full switch.
[04:57] Maya Chen: we have built-in rollout controls — canary percentages, auto-rollback on quality regression tied to eval prompt sets. You can attach a prompt set and a pass/fail threshold.
[05:11] Priya Singh: speaking of evals, can you ingest our internal prompts so we can automatically run A/B quality comparisons?
[05:17] Maya Chen: yes, you can upload a prompt bundle or link to an S3 bucket and Optimize will run side-by-side comparisons and flag regressions.
[05:27] Samir Das: network egress — if we go Dedicated in a cloud region, can we keep traffic inside our VPC?
[05:33] Jordan Patel: for Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and private link patterns, so no public egress required. We'll map the network architecture for your infra team in the follow-up.
[05:44] Alex Rivera: latency SLOs — can Redwood guarantee 95th pct lat for our short chat prompts?
[05:51] Maya Chen: with Dedicated capacity and tuned batching, yes we hit strict SLOs. For hosted, we publish performance profiles but for guaranteed SLOs we'd recommend Dedicated. We can also do a short benchmark run to validate for your workload.
[06:04] Priya Singh: about billing and quotas — how are bursts handled? we occasionally have spikes during morning syncs.
[06:11] Jordan Patel: we offer burst lanes on Dedicated and auto-burst credits for hosted. In the pricing pack we'll show committed capacity plus burst pricing.
[06:21] Maya Chen: showing the parity mapping spreadsheet now — columns: source provider, source model, Redwood variant, expected perf delta, tokenization notes, recommended quant profile, sample prompt adjustments.
[06:34] Priya Singh: can you pre-fill some rows for our top 10 prompts? that would speed up evaluation.
[06:39] Jordan Patel: absolutely, if you send your top prompts Maya can annotate and we'll pre-populate the sheet.
[06:45] Alex Rivera: timeline — we want to decide by end of month for a Q1 pilot. Is that realistic?
[06:52] Jordan Patel: yes, totally — typical path is 1) parity mapping and bench run (1-2 weeks), 2) pilot on Dedicated sandbox (2-4 weeks), 3) expand to prod. We can compress it if you have engineers ready to run tests.
[07:06] Samir Das: SAML SSO for console access — our SecOps needs SSO and RBAC.
[07:11] Maya Chen: we support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for user sync, RBAC is role-based and audit logs are available per route.
[07:20] Priya Singh: any gotchas when moving streaming sessions from Together to Redwood?
[07:25] Maya Chen: sometimes chunk semantics differ, but we expose chunk size and timeouts so you can match behavior. We'll also recommend front-end buffering changes if necessary.
[07:36] Alex Rivera: okay, this is helpful. Could you also provide an estimate for cost savings if we quantize the summarization pipeline?
[07:44] Jordan Patel: yes, we'll include a modeled savings estimate in the parity sheet based on your traffic sample. Rough back-of-envelope numbers often show 20-40% token cost reduction depending on model and quantization.
[07:58] Priya Singh: do you have a reference for previous customers that did similar migration? internal case studies?
[08:04] Jordan Patel: we have anonymized case studies and benchmark results — I'll attach the customer story deck.
[08:12] Samir Das: last question on data retention — we need logs deleted after 90 days and ability to opt-out of storing prompts.
[08:20] Jordan Patel: configurable retention windows are available; Private gives you full control. For hosted we offer retention config and options for non-persistent modes.
[08:31] Alex Rivera: great. sounds like next concrete items are parity spreadsheet, benchmark, and security pack.
[08:36] Jordan Patel: perfect. Maya any final console pointers?
[08:40] Maya Chen: just that you'll get a sandbox link, and the Optimize tab will surface suggested batch sizes per route after the first few runs. Also watch the eval regression alerts — they can auto-fail a rollout.
[08:52] Priya Singh: thanks all — Priya here, i'll email the prompt bundle and traffic sample by tomorrow.
[08:58] Jordan Patel: awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and a booking link for the benchmark slot.
[09:05] Alex Rivera: thanks, bye.
